LESSON: FLUENCY: PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Fluency: Pronunciation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fluency: Pronunciation, part of Strand 1 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to speak clearly? 2. How do we learn correct pronunciation of words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to recorded clips on articulation and pronunciation of words and repeat saying them,

2. record each other as they pronounce words and peer review for correctness,

3. take turns to select thematic vocabulary and nouns from a word basket and use them to create sentences,

4. engage in language games to identify synonyms of words,

5. team up with peers to organise an indigenous languages debate contest related to the theme using acquired vocabulary, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to recorded clips on articulation and pronunciation of words and repeat saying them,
2. record each other as they pronounce words and peer review for correctness,
3. take turns to select thematic vocabulary and nouns from a word basket and use them to create sentences,
4. engage in language games to identify synonyms of words,
5. team up with peers to organise an indigenous languages debate contest related to the theme using acquired vocabulary, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fluency: Pronunciation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: This is developed as the learner is motivated to learn continuously as they listen to recorded clips on

articulation and pronunciation of words and repeats saying them.

• Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner shows defining personal skills when teaming up with peers to organise an

indigenous languages debate contest related to the theme.

Values:
• Respect: This is developed as the learner accommodates diverse opinions during the debate contest.

• Social justice: This is enhanced as the learner accords equal opportunities to peers when taking turns to select thematic

vocabulary from a word basket.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Nationalism: This is promoted as the learner interacts with peers during the debate to share opinions and with views on a topic

related to peace building.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of peace building to the concept of living together as is covered in Religious Education.
